params.desc: number of bytes to write. The values must be a multiple of 4096

params.name: source

params.name: fmt
params.desc: Output parameter; format of the bitmap

params.name: palette

name: EVE_CoCmd_getMatrix
signature: bool EVE_CoCmd_getMatrix(EVE_HalContext *phost, int32_t *m)
summary: This command retrieves the current matrix within the context of the coprocessor engine

name: EVE_CoCmd_getProps
signature: bool EVE_CoCmd_getProps(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t *ptr, uint32_t *width, uint32_t *height)
summary: This command returns the source address and size of the bitmap loaded by the previous CMD_LOADIMAGE

params.name: width
params.desc: The width of the image which is decoded by the last CMD_LOADIMAGE before this command

params.name: height
params.desc: The height of the image which is decoded by the last CMD_LOADIMAGE before this command

name: EVE_CoCmd_getPtr
signature: bool EVE_CoCmd_getPtr(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t *result)
summary: This command returns to the first unallocated memory location

params.name: result
params.desc: Pointer to the first unallocated memory location

name: EVE_CoCmd_gradColor
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_gradColor(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t c)
summary: This command is used to set the 3D Button Highlight Color

params.name: c
params.desc: New highlight gradient color, as a 24-bit RGB number. White is the default value, i.e., 0xFFFFFF. Red is the most significant 8 bits, blue is the least. So 0xFF0000 is bright red. Gradient is supported only for Button and Keys widgets

name: EVE_CoCmd_gradient
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_gradient(EVE_HalContext *phost, int16_t x0, int16_t y0, uint32_t rgb0, int16_t x1, int16_t y1, uint32_t rgb1)
summary: This command is used to create a smooth transition between color gradients

params.name: rgb0
params.desc: Color of point 0, as a 24-bit RGB number. Red is the most significant 8 bits, Blue is the least. So 0xff0000 is bright red

params.name: rgb1
params.desc: Color of point 1, as a 24-bit RGB number. Red is the most significant 8 bits, Blue is the least. So 0xff0000 is bright red

name: EVE_CoCmd_gradientA
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_gradientA(EVE_HalContext *phost, int16_t x0, int16_t y0, uint32_t argb0, int16_t x1, int16_t y1, uint32_t argb1)
summary: This command is used to draw a smooth color gradient with transparency

params.name: argb0
params.desc: color of point 0, as a 32-bit ARGB number. A is the most significant 8 bits, B is the least. So 0x80ff0000 is 50% transparent bright red, and 0xff0000ff is solid blue.

params.name: argb1
params.desc: color of point 1, as a 32-bit ARGB number. A is the most significant 8 bits, B is the least. So 0x80ff0000 is 50% transparent bright red, and 0xff0000ff is solid blue.

name: EVE_CoCmd_hsf
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_hsf(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t hsf)
summary: This command sets the horizontal scale factor for the graphics engine

params.name: hsf
params.desc: Output pixel width. The value must be less than REG_HSIZE. Setting it to 0 disables HSF

name: EVE_CoCmd_inflate
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_inflate(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr)
summary: This command decompresses the specified compressed data into RAM_G. The data must be compressed using the DEFLATE algorithm, such as with the ZLIB library. This command is especially useful for loading graphics data

params.name: ptr
params.desc: Destination address in RAM_G. The data byte should immediately follow in the command buffer.

name: EVE_CoCmd_inflate2
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_inflate2(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr, uint32_t options)
summary: This command decompresses the specified compressed data into RAM_G. The data may be supplied via the command buffer, the media FIFO, or from flash memory. It must be compressed using the DEFLATE algorithm, such as with the ZLIB library. This command is especially useful for loading graphics data

params.name: ptr
params.desc: destination address to put the decompressed data

params.name: options
params.desc: If the option OPT_MEDIAFIFO is specified, the compressed data is sourced from the media FIFO. If the option OPT_FLASH is specified, the data is read from flash memory. When using flash as the source, CMD_FLASHSOURCE must be called before this command to specify the source address. Otherwise, a zero value should be given, and the compressed data must immediately follow

name: EVE_CoCmd_interrupt
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_interrupt(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ms)
summary: This command is used to trigger the CMDFLAG Interrupt

params.name: ms
params.desc: The delay before the interrupt triggers, in milliseconds. The interrupt is guaranteed not to fire before this delay. If ms is zero the interrupt fires immediately

name: EVE_CoCmd_keys
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_keys(EVE_HalContext *phost, int16_t x, int16_t y, int16_t w, int16_t h, uint16_t font, uint16_t options, const char *s)
summary: This command is used to draw a row of keys

params.name: x
params.desc: x-coordinate of keys top-left, in pixels

params.name: y
params.desc: y-coordinate of keys top-left, in pixels

params.name: font
params.desc: Bitmap handle to specify the font used in key label. The valid range is from 0 to 63

params.name: options
params.desc: By default, keys are drawn with a 3D effect, and the option value is zero. Specifying OPT_FLAT removes the 3D effect. If OPT_CENTER is set, the keys are drawn at their minimum size, centered within the w x h rectangle. Otherwise, the keys are expanded to fully fill the available space. If an ASCII code is provided, that key is drawn in a ‘'pressed’' state–- using the background color with any 3D effect removed

params.name: s
params.desc: key labels, one character per key. The TAG value is set to the ASCII value of each key, so that key presses can be detected using the REG_TOUCH_TAG register.

name: EVE_CoCmd_loadIdentity
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_loadIdentity(EVE_HalContext *phost)
summary: This command instructs the coprocessor engine to set the current matrix to the identity matrix, so that the coprocessor engine can form the new matrix as requested by CMD_SCALE, CMD_ROTATE and CMD_TRANSLATE command

name: EVE_CoCmd_loadImage
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_loadImage(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr, uint32_t options)
summary: This command loads a JPEG or PNG image, decompressing the provided JPEG or PNG image data into a specific EVE bitmap format stored in RAM_G

params.name: options
desc: OPT_MONO - loaded in L8 format; OPT_TRUECOLOR - loaded in RGB565 format
OPT_FULLSCREEN Scales the bitmap to fill as much of the screen as possible
OPT_FLASH: Uses flash memory as the source for the image data
OPT_MEDIAFIFO - Uses the media FIFO as the source for the image data

name: EVE_CoCmd_logo
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_logo(EVE_HalContext *phost)
summary: The logo command causes the coprocessor engine to play back a short animation of the Bridgetek logo

name: EVE_CoCmd_mediaFifo
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_mediaFifo(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr, uint32_t size)
summary: This command is to set up a streaming media FIFO. Allocate the specified area of RAM_G and set it up as streaming media FIFO

params.name: size
params.desc: number of bytes of media FIFO

name: EVE_CoCmd_memCpy
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_memCpy(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t dest, uint32_t src, uint32_t num)
summary: This command is used to copy a block of memory

params.name: dest

params.name: src
params.desc: address of the source memory block

name: EVE_CoCmd_memCrc
signature: bool EVE_CoCmd_memCrc(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr, uint32_t num, uint32_t *result)
summary: This command computes a CRC-32 for a block of RAM_G memory

params.name: ptr

params.name: num

params.name: result
params.desc: Output parameter; written with the CRC-32 after command execution

name: EVE_CoCmd_memSet
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_memSet(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr, uint32_t value, uint32_t num)
summary: This command is used to fill a block of memory with a byte value

params.name: ptr
params.desc: Starting address of the memory block

params.name: value

params.name: num
params.desc: Number of bytes in the memory block

name: EVE_CoCmd_memWrite

summary: This command writes the following bytes into the memory

params.name: ptr

params.name: num
params.desc: Number of bytes to be written

name: EVE_CoCmd_memWrite32
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_memWrite32(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr, uint32_t value)

params.name: ptr
params.desc: The memory address to be written

name: EVE_CoCmd_memZero
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_memZero(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr, uint32_t num)

params.name: ptr
params.desc: starting address of the memory block

params.name: num
params.desc: number of bytes in the memory block

name: EVE_CoCmd_newList
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_newList(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t a)
summary: This command starts the compilation of a command list into RAM_G

params.name: a
params.desc: memory address of start of command list

name: EVE_CoCmd_nop
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_nop(EVE_HalContext *phost)
summary: The nop command does nothing

name: EVE_CoCmd_number
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_number(EVE_HalContext *phost, int16_t x, int16_t y, uint16_t font, uint16_t options, int32_t n)
summary: This command is used to draw a number

params.name: x
params.desc: x-coordinate of text base, in pixels

params.name: y
params.desc: y-coordinate of text base, in pixels

params.name: options
params.desc: By default (x,y) is the top-left pixel of the text. OPT_CENTERX centers the text horizontally; OPT_CENTERY centers it vertically; OPT_CENTER centers the text in both directions; OPT_RIGHTX right-justifies the text, so that the x is the rightmost pixel.

params.name: n
params.desc: The number to display is either unsigned or signed 32-bit, in the base specified in the preceding CMD_SETBASE.If no CMD_SETBASE appears before CMD_NUMBER, it will be in decimal base

name: EVE_CoCmd_pclkFreq
signature: uint32_t EVE_CoCmd_pclkFreq(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ftarget, int32_t rounding)
summary: This command sets REG_PCLK_FREQ to generate the closest possible pixel clock frequency to the requested value. If no suitable frequency can be found, the result field is zero and REG_PCLK_FREQ remains unchanged

params.name: ftarget
params.desc: Target pixel clock frequency, in Hertz (Hz).

params.name: rounding
params.desc: Approximation mode. Valid values are: 0 - nearest, -1 - highest frequency less than or equal to target, 1 - lowest frequency greater than or equal to target.

name: EVE_CoCmd_playVideo
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_playVideo(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t options)
summary: Plays back MJPEG-encoded AVI video. The playback starts immediately, and the command completes when playback ends. The playback may be paused or terminated by writing to 32-bit register REG_PLAY_CONTROL

params.name: options
desc: OPT_FULLSCREEN: Zooms the video to fill as much of the screen as possible.
OPT_SOUND: Decodes the audio data, if present, following the video data.
OPT_OVERLAY: Appends the video bitmap to an existing display list rather than starting a new display list.
OPT_MEDIAFIFO: AVI video data from the media FIFO in RAM_G instead of the command buffer.
OPT_FLASH: Sources video data from flash. When using flash CMD_FLASHSOURCE must be called before this command to specify the source address
OPT_NOTEAR: Synchronizes video updates to the display blanking interval to avoid horizontal tearing artifacts
OPT_NODL: Does not modify the current display list. A display list rendering the video bitmap must already exist

name: EVE_CoCmd_progress
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_progress(EVE_HalContext *phost, int16_t x, int16_t y, int16_t w, int16_t h, uint16_t options, uint16_t val, uint16_t range)
summary: This command is used to draw a progress bar

params.name: x
params.desc: x-coordinate of progress bar top-left, in pixels

params.name: y
params.desc: y-coordinate of progress bar top-left, in pixels

params.name: w
params.desc: Width of the progress bar, in pixels

params.name: h
params.desc: Height of the progress bar, in pixels

params.name: options
params.desc: By default, the progress bar is drawn with a 3D effect and options value is set to zero. The OPT_FLAT option removes the 3D effect and has a value of 256.

params.name: val
params.desc: Displayed value of progress bar, between 0 and range inclusive

params.name: range
params.desc: Maximum value of the progress bar

name: EVE_CoCmd_regRead
signature: bool EVE_CoCmd_regRead(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr, uint32_t *result)
summary: This command reads a register value

params.name: ptr
params.desc: Address of the register to be read

params.name: result
params.desc: The register value which has been read from the ptr address OUTPUT parameter. Write a dummy 32-bit value 0x00000000 for this parameter and the Co-Processor will replace this value with the result after the command has been executed. After execution, the host should then reads the address of this parameter in RAM_CMD to get the result value

name: EVE_CoCmd_romFont

name: EVE_CoCmd_rotate
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_rotate(EVE_HalContext *phost, int32_t a)

params.name: a
params.desc: Clockwise rotation angle, in units of 1/65536 of a circle

name: EVE_CoCmd_rotateAround
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_rotateAround(EVE_HalContext *phost, int32_t x, int32_t y, uint32_t a, int32_t s)
summary: This command is used to apply a rotation and scale around a specified coordinate

params.name: a
params.desc: clockwise rotation angle, in units of 1/65536 of a circle

params.name: s
params.desc: scale factor, in signed 16.16 bit fixed-point form

name: EVE_CoCmd_runAnim
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_runAnim(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t waitmask, uint32_t play)
summary: This command is used to play/run animations until complete

params.name: waitmask
params.desc: 32-bit mask specifying which animation channels to wait for. Animation ends when the logical AND of this mask and REG_ANIM_ACTIVE is zero

params.name: play
params.desc: Address of play control byte. Animation stops when the byte at play is not zero. If this feature is not required, the special value of -1 (0xFFFF FFFF) means that there is no control byte

name: EVE_CoCmd_scale
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_scale(EVE_HalContext *phost, int32_t sx, int32_t sy)
summary: This command is used to apply a scaling transformation to the current matrix.

params.name: sx
params.desc: x scale factor, in signed 16.16 bit fixed-point form.

params.name: sy
params.desc: y scale factor, in signed 16.16 bit fixed-point form

name: EVE_CoCmd_screenSaver
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_screenSaver(EVE_HalContext *phost)
summary: This command is used to start an animated screensaver

name: EVE_CoCmd_scrollbar

summary: This command is used to draw a scroll bar

params.name: x
params.desc: x-coordinate of scroll bar top-left, in pixels

params.desc: y-coordinate of scroll bar top-left, in pixels

params.name: w
params.desc: Width of scroll bar, in pixels. If width is greater than height, the scroll bar is drawn horizontally

params.name: h
params.desc: Height of scroll bar, in pixels. If height is greater than width, the scroll bar is drawn vertically

params.name: val
params.desc: Displayed value of scroll bar, between 0 and range inclusive

name: EVE_CoCmd_setBase
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_setBase(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t base)
summary: This command is used to set the base for number output

params.name: base
params.desc: Numeric base, valid values are from 2 to 36: 2 for binary, 8 for octal, 10 for decimal, 16 for hexadecimal

name: EVE_CoCmd_setBitmap
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_setBitmap(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t source, uint16_t fmt, uint16_t width, uint16_t height)
summary: This command generates the appropriate display list commands based on the provided bitmap information, eliminating the need to manually write the display list

params.name: source
params.desc: Source address for bitmap, in RAM_G or from SWAPCHAIN_1 (0xFFFF01FF) or from SWAPCHAIN_2 (0xFFFF02FF), as a BITMAP_SOURCE parameter

params.name: fmt
params.desc: Bitmap format, see the definition in BITMAP_EXT_FORMAT

params.name: width

params.name: height
params.desc: bitmap height, in pixels. 2 bytes value

name: EVE_CoCmd_setFont
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_setFont(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t font, uint32_t ptr)
summary: CMD_SETFONT is used to register a custom-defined bitmap font with the coprocessor engine. Once registered, the coprocessor engine can use the bitmap font with the appropriate commands

params.name: ptr
params.desc: The address of the metrics block in RAM_G. Must be 4-byte aligned.

name: EVE_CoCmd_setFont2
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_setFont2(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t font, uint32_t ptr, uint32_t firstchar)
summary: This command is used to set up a custom font. To use a custom font with the coprocessor objects, create the font definition data in RAM_G and issue CMD_SETFONT2, as described in ROM and RAM Fonts

params.name: ptr
params.desc: 32 bits aligned memory address in RAM_G of font metrics block

params.name: firstchar

name: EVE_CoCmd_setMatrix
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_setMatrix(EVE_HalContext *phost)

name: EVE_CoCmd_setRotate

params.name: r

name: EVE_CoCmd_setScratch
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_setScratch(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t handle)
summary: This command is used to set the scratch bitmap for widget use

name: EVE_CoCmd_sketch

params.name: x

name: EVE_CoCmd_snapshot
signature: void EVE_CoCmd_snapshot(EVE_HalContext *phost, uint32_t ptr)

name: EVE_CoCmd_snapshot2

name: EVE_CoCmd_stop

name: EVE_CoCmd_swap

summary: This command is used to draw a UTF-8 Text string
